subject: Q3 pilot: guaranteed cold-start lanes for Atlas Health demo
messages:
From: Rajeev Menon <rajeev@atlashealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Megan Li <megan.li@cloudpartner.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask — guaranteed lanes for Q3 customer demo

Marcus,

Thanks again for the onboarding call this week. Atlas Health is targeting a live demo for their execs on July 7 and we need a short (3 business day) window of predictable latency for the demo flows. Our product team is sensitive to cold-starts — during prior pilots we saw 300–400ms spikes when model instances were scaled up.

Can Redwood provide a short reservation or an autoscaling exception that guarantees warm instances (or a minimum of 4 GPU slots) during July 6–8? We understand this is an exception to the standard autoscaling policy and are happy to sign reasonable terms/credits.

I've attached our SLO spreadsheet and a short security checklist for procurement. Happy to walk through requirements tomorrow.

Attachments: Atlas_Pilot_SLOs.xlsx (xlsx), Atlas_Security_Reqs.pdf (pdf)

—Rajeev
Head of Integrations, Atlas Health
rajeev@atlashealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajeev Menon <rajeev@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — guaranteed lanes for Q3 customer demo

Rajeev — thanks for the clear ask and the files. Copying in Kimberly (capacity/product operations) and Lauren (sales ops) so we can scope impact and confirm feasibility.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provision a short reservation on Dedicated that pins a minimum of GPU capacity for a date window, but we need to confirm exact model family and concurrency assumptions.
- Autoscaling exceptions are possible but gated: they require an ops runbook, run-time guardrails (TTL, failback policy), and signoff from capacity stewardship.

Kimberly / Neha — can you confirm whether a 4-GPU minimum for July 6–8 is doable in the us-west pool given current committed capacity? If it’s tight, what are trade-offs (preemptible vs reserved buffer, guaranteed vs warm-prefetch)?

Lauren — procurement note: Rajeev mentioned willingness to sign credits/terms; can your team draft a short one-week reservation addendum to attach to the pilot MSA? I’ve included the HubSpot deal id below.

Action items I propose:
1) Ops feasibility check (Kimberly/Neha) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Draft addendum (Lauren) by Mon 6/14.
3) If feasible, we create a pre-warm runbook + rollback (ops) and a short customer-facing note describing expected SLOs.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the feasibility check and we can escalate to capacity stewardship if required.

—Marcus
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rajeev Menon <rajeev@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — guaranteed lanes for Q3 customer demo

Hi all — did a quick capacity sweep for the us-west dedicated pools. Short answer: we can support a 4-GPU pinned reservation for July 6–8 but with two caveats:

1) Trade-off on burst capacity: if we pin 4 GPUs as reserved for Atlas, it reduces available burst capacity for other enterprise pilots that week. We can mitigate by authorizing a temporary pre-warm policy (warm-prefetch) that keeps kernels/hot cache loaded only for the scheduled demo hours (2 hours/day).

2) Ops guardrails required: we need a runbook that includes (a) TTL auto-release at 23:59 PDT on July 8, (b) automatic failback to the shared pool if we detect >20% unused capacity for 2 consecutive hours, and (c) a one-click rollback to free capacity in case of emergency.

If Atlas agrees to those guardrails and the short addendum, I’ll file the reservation and set up the pre-warm job. Estimated ops time: ~4 hours to stage + 1 hour to validate pre-warm behavior. If they want full 24/7 warm instances, we’d need a larger committed slice and discuss pricing.

Rajeev — can you confirm the demo start times (local) and which models you will serve (gptx-7b family or gptx-13b)? That drives the memory and kernel warm-up plan.

Kimberly
Capacity & Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rajeev Menon <rajeev@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — guaranteed lanes for Q3 customer demo

Chiming in with procurement and timeline: Atlas Procurement has the security checklist and SLO spreadsheet. They said they can sign a one-week reservation addendum (simple amendment) but need it attached to the MSA by June 21 to get legal approval in time. I’ve drafted a short addendum that:
- lists July 6–8, 2027 as the reservation window
- specifies a 4-GPU minimum in us-west dedicated pool
- references Kimberly’s ops guardrails (TTL + failback + rollback)
- includes a credits clause: if we fail to meet the pre-warm SLOs during the demo hours, Atlas gets a one-time credit equal to one day of the reserved cost

Link to draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AtlasPilotDocs (Docs: "Atlas_Reservation_Addendum_v1")

Next steps: Marcus — if you approve, I’ll attach the addendum to HubSpot (HubSpot:HS-584921) and loop legal. Kimberly/Neha — please send me the exact model family and time windows once confirmed so I can lock language.

—Lauren
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
